figures.alt: Photo of a mother deer and her spotted fawn standing among ferns in a forest.
figures.caption: A fawn (a baby deer) looks like its mother, but it has spots that its mother does not have.

figures.alt: Close photo of a spiky burr stuck to a gray wool sock, with its tiny hooks caught in the knit.
figures.caption: A burr has tiny hooks that grab fabric. People copied that idea to make hook-and-loop fasteners (straps with hooks on one side and loops on the other).

figures.alt: Photo of a mother mallard duck walking at a pond edge followed by four ducklings in a line.
figures.caption: A mother mallard, a common Michigan pond duck, walks with her ducklings. The ducklings follow her.
